intent.raw_query: Morocco Marrakech and Sahara, $1000 solo, 7 days, March 2026

selected_hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, Morocco (Marrakech and Sahara)

experiences.name: Explore Djemaa el-Fna Square
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in the beating heart of Marrakech at this UNESCO-listed square. Watch snake charmers, storytellers, acrobats, and musicians perform as the sun sets. Sample street food like msemen flatbread, harira soup, and fresh orange juice from the surrounding stalls.

experiences.name: Overnight Sahara Desert Camel Trek & Bivouac Camp
experiences.description: Ride camels into the golden Erg Chebbi dunes at sunset, arriving at a traditional Berber bivouac camp. Enjoy a tagine dinner under a sky full of stars, listen to Gnawa music around the campfire, and wake at dawn to watch the sunrise paint the dunes in shades of orange and red.

experiences.name: Medina Souk Walking Tour & Tanneries Visit
experiences.description: Navigate the labyrinthine souks of the ancient Medina with a local guide, discovering artisan workshops for leather, ceramics, and spices. Visit the iconic Chouara Tannery to witness the centuries-old leather dyeing process from a rooftop terrace overlooking the colorful vats.

experiences.name: Bahia Palace & Saadian Tombs Historical Tour
experiences.description: Step back into Morocco's imperial past with a self-guided tour of the stunning 19th-century Bahia Palace, featuring intricate zellige tilework and carved cedar ceilings. Then visit the Saadian Tombs, a hidden royal necropolis dating to the 16th century, rediscovered only in 1917.

experiences.name: Moroccan Cooking Class in a Riad
experiences.description: Join a hands-on cooking class hosted inside a traditional riad courtyard. Visit the local market with your host to select fresh spices and ingredients, then learn to prepare classic Moroccan dishes including chicken tagine with preserved lemon, couscous, and bastilla pastry.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Morocco (Marrakech and Sahara)
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, Morocco (Marrakech and Sahara)

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Marrakech Menara Airport at 22:30. Take a petit taxi (negotiate fare, roughly 70-100 MAD) to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and get a good night's rest to prepare for the week ahead.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport
meals.dinner: Grab a quick snack from a convenience stall near the airport or hotel — try a msemen flatbread or a small harira soup from a local night vendor (5-15 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: Keep some Moroccan dirhams (MAD) ready upon arrival for taxi and tips. Exchange currency at the airport or use an ATM — avoid hotel exchange desks for better rates. Confirm hotel check-in details in advance since arrival is late.

day_by_day.morning: Start the day with a stroll into the heart of Marrakech's UNESCO-listed Medina. Visit the iconic Djemaa el-Fna square in the morning when it's quieter and atmospheric. Explore the nearby souks (markets) of spices, leather, and crafts. Head to the Koutoubia Mosque gardens for a peaceful walk and photos of the 12th-century minaret (non-Muslims view from outside, free).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Bahia Palace (entrance ~70 MAD) — a stunning 19th-century riad palace with intricate Moroccan tilework, carved cedar ceilings, and lush gardens. Afterward, explore the mellah (Jewish quarter) and its old synagogues for a slice of multicultural Moroccan history.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Djemaa el-Fna at dusk when it transforms into a massive open-air spectacle with snake charmers, storytellers, acrobats, and food stalls. Enjoy the electric atmosphere and people-watch from a rooftop café terrace overlooking the square.

meals.breakfast: Café de France or a local café near the Medina — mint tea, msemen, and amlou (almond-argan dip) for around 25-40 MAD
meals.lunch: Eat at one of the small Medina eateries — try a tagine with bread or a harira soup with dates for 40-60 MAD
meals.dinner: Djemaa el-Fna food stalls — try merguez sausages, grilled kefta, and fresh-squeezed orange juice for 50-80 MAD total

day_by_day.notes: Bargaining is expected in the souks — start at 30-40% of the asking price. Be cautious of unsolicited 'guides' who may lead you into shops for commissions. Wear comfortable shoes for cobblestone streets.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Saadian Tombs (entrance ~70 MAD) — a hidden 16th-century royal necropolis rediscovered in 1917, featuring beautifully decorated mausoleums. Then walk to the El Badi Palace ruins (entrance ~70 MAD), a once-magnificent 16th-century palace now a sprawling atmospheric ruin with resident storks nesting on the walls.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Mellah market and pick up affordable local snacks and dried fruits. Head to the Jardin Majorelle (entrance ~100 MAD for gardens, extra for Berber Museum) — a stunning cobalt-blue botanical garden once owned by Yves Saint Laurent. Alternatively, visit the free Cyber Park Arsat Moulay Abdeslam for a relaxing green space if budget is tight.
day_by_day.evening: Take an evening cooking class or simply explore the artisan quarter near Bab Doukkala. Visit a local hammam (public bathhouse) for an authentic Moroccan experience — a basic hammam costs as little as 15-30 MAD, or a tourist-friendly option like Hammam Dar el-Bacha for ~150 MAD with scrub included.

meals.breakfast: At the hotel or a local patisserie — café au lait, croissant, and fresh orange juice for 20-35 MAD
meals.lunch: Lunch at a small riad restaurant in the Medina — try pastilla (sweet pigeon pie) or couscous for 50-80 MAD
meals.dinner: Try Restaurant Souk Kafe or a similar budget riad eatery — a full Moroccan set menu for 80-120 MAD

day_by_day.notes: Jardin Majorelle can get crowded by midday — try to arrive right when it opens. The hammam experience is a must-do cultural activity; bring flip-flops and a change of clothes.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Marrakech early (around 7:00-8:00 AM) via a shared CTM bus or a budget group tour toward the Sahara Desert — the journey to Merzouga (gateway to Erg Chebbi dunes) takes approximately 9-10 hours via Ouarzazate and the Draa Valley. Book a budget group desert tour in advance (typically 350-600 MAD per person including transport, camel ride, and desert camp). Enjoy dramatic Atlas Mountain scenery along the way.
day_by_day.afternoon: Pass through the stunning Draa Valley with its palm groves and kasbahs, and stop at the famous Aït Benhaddou kasbah (a UNESCO World Heritage Site used in Game of Thrones and Gladiator) if your tour includes it — entrance ~10 MAD. Continue through the Dadès Gorge area with towering red rock formations.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at the edge of the Erg Chebbi dunes near Merzouga at sunset. Mount camels for a magical 1-hour trek into the Sahara Desert as the sun sets over the golden dunes. Arrive at a budget desert camp (included in tour package or approximately 200-300 MAD per person for a basic Berber camp with dinner and breakfast).

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at hotel before departure — bread, olive oil, and mint tea
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or stop at a roadside tagine restaurant along the route — 40-60 MAD
meals.dinner: Traditional Berber dinner at the desert camp — tagine, couscous, and mint tea under the stars (typically included in camp fee)

day_by_day.notes: Book your Sahara group tour 2-3 days in advance from Marrakech — compare prices at Djemaa el-Fna tour desks or via hostel notice boards. Pack a warm layer — desert nights in March can drop to 5-10°C. Bring sunscreen, a headscarf, and a reusable water bottle.

day_by_day.morning: Wake before sunrise (around 6:00 AM) to climb the Erg Chebbi dunes on foot for a breathtaking desert sunrise — one of Morocco's most spectacular experiences. Watch the shifting colors of the sand from orange to gold. After breakfast at camp, explore the village of Merzouga on foot or by bicycle (rentals ~50 MAD/day) and visit a local Gnawa music community.
day_by_day.afternoon: Optional adventure activities near Merzouga: sandboarding on the dunes (boards available at camp for ~50 MAD), or a quad bike excursion (budget options from ~200 MAD for 1 hour). Alternatively, visit a nomadic Berber family nearby for tea and a glimpse into traditional desert life — often free or a small voluntary contribution.
day_by_day.evening: Begin the return journey toward Marrakech or overnight in a budget guesthouse in Merzouga or Rissani (~100-150 MAD per night). If staying, enjoy a relaxed evening stargazing in one of the world's clearest night skies, far from light pollution.

meals.breakfast: Included at desert camp — Berber bread, honey, olive oil, and mint tea
meals.lunch: Local restaurant in Merzouga village — camel meat tagine or vegetable couscous for 50-70 MAD
meals.dinner: Budget guesthouse dinner or a local family restaurant — a hearty Moroccan meal for 60-90 MAD

day_by_day.notes: The Erg Chebbi dunes reach up to 150 meters — climbing is strenuous but rewarding. Start the ascent slowly and stay hydrated. If returning to Marrakech same day, expect a very long journey — an overnight in Merzouga is strongly recommended for comfort.

day_by_day.morning: Return journey from the Sahara toward Marrakech via a scenic alternate route through the Todra Gorge (a spectacular 300-meter-high limestone canyon) — a short detour well worth the extra time. Walk along the gorge floor between the towering rock walls (free entry). Local cafés at the gorge base serve mint tea with incredible views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the drive back through the High Atlas Mountains, passing through Kelaat M'Gouna (Valley of Roses, famous for its rose festival in May) and the scenic Ouarzazate, sometimes called the 'Hollywood of Africa.' If time permits, visit the Atlas Film Studios (entrance ~80 MAD) where Lawrence of Arabia, Gladiator, and many others were filmed.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back in Marrakech by early evening. Rest at the hotel, then take a final leisurely walk through the Medina for last-minute souvenir shopping. Visit a local artisan cooperative where prices are fixed and fair — look for leather goods, argan oil, and Berber rugs.

meals.breakfast: At the guesthouse in Merzouga or a roadside café — bread, jam, and coffee for 20-30 MAD
meals.lunch: Café at Todra Gorge — tagine or omelette with bread for 50-70 MAD
meals.dinner: Back in Marrakech — try a local Medina restaurant for a farewell Moroccan feast; chicken tagine with preserved lemon for 70-100 MAD

day_by_day.notes: The Todra Gorge is best visited in the morning light. The road through the Atlas Mountains can be winding — take motion sickness medication if needed. Ouarzazate is a good place to fuel up and stretch before the final push to Marrakech.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Marrakech — visit the Musée de Marrakech (entrance ~50 MAD), housed in a beautifully restored 19th-century palace with Moroccan art and artifacts. Wander through the quieter northern Medina alleys near the Medersa Ben Youssef (entrance ~70 MAD) — a stunning 14th-century Islamic college with intricate zellij tilework and carved stucco.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute souvenir shopping in the souks — pick up affordable gifts like spices, argan oil, leather poufs, or hand-painted ceramics. Head back to the hotel to collect luggage and check out. Take a petit taxi or negotiate a shared transfer to Marrakech Menara Airport (allow at least 1.5-2 hours before departure for check-in and security).
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Marrakech. Reflect on an incredible week of culture, history, desert adventure, and authentic Moroccan experiences.

meals.breakfast: Final Moroccan breakfast at a Medina café — bissara (fava bean soup), bread, and mint tea for 25-40 MAD
meals.lunch: Quick lunch near the Medersa — a sandwich or bocadillo from a street vendor for 15-25 MAD
meals.dinner: Airport dining or in-flight meal

day_by_day.notes: Marrakech airport can be busy — arrive at least 2 hours before departure. Use remaining dirhams on airport snacks or last-minute gifts, as MAD is not easily exchangeable outside Morocco. Keep a small amount of cash for airport tips and taxi. Confirm return flight details the night before.

trip_options.title: Classic Morocco (Marrakech and Sahara) Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, Morocco (Marrakech and Sahara)

day_by_day.morning: No activities — flight in transit
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities — flight in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Marrakech Menara Airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. Pre-arranged airport transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and settle into your room. Grab a light late-night snack from the hotel if available.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at departure airport
meals.lunch: On the plane or at layover airport
meals.dinner: Late-night hotel snack or room service upon arrival — keep it light after a long travel day

day_by_day.notes: Arrival is at 22:30, so no sightseeing is planned. Allow at least 45–60 minutes for immigration, baggage claim, and transfer. Confirm your airport pickup in advance. Rest well — a full day of exploration begins tomorrow.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely hotel breakfast to recover from travel. Afterward, head into the heart of Marrakech's Medina. Explore the iconic Djemaa el-Fna square in the morning calm before the crowds arrive. Visit the nearby Koutoubia Mosque (exterior) and stroll through the surrounding gardens.
day_by_day.afternoon: Dive into the labyrinthine souks of the Medina — explore the spice market (Rahba Kedima), leather goods alley, and the famous Chouara Tanneries viewpoint. Visit the beautifully ornate Ben Youssef Madrasa, one of Morocco's finest examples of Islamic architecture and scholarship.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Djemaa el-Fna at sunset to experience its legendary transformation — street performers, storytellers, snake charmers, and food stalls light up the square. Enjoy dinner at one of the rooftop restaurants overlooking the square.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort — included or buffet style
meals.lunch: Café des Épices near Rahba Kedima — mid-range Moroccan plates, great rooftop views, try the tagine or kefta sandwich (approx. 80–120 MAD)
meals.dinner: Le Marrakchi or a similar rooftop restaurant on Djemaa el-Fna — traditional Moroccan feast with couscous, pastilla, and mint tea (approx. 150–250 MAD per person)

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes — the Medina streets are uneven. Modest dress is recommended near religious sites. Bargaining in souks is expected and part of the culture — start at 40–50% of the asking price. Keep small change handy for tips.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the stunning Bahia Palace, a 19th-century masterpiece of Moroccan architecture with intricate tilework, carved cedar ceilings, and lush gardens. Follow up with a visit to the El Badi Palace ruins — a hauntingly beautiful reminder of the Saadian dynasty's former glory.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Saadian Tombs, a remarkable necropolis hidden for centuries and rediscovered in 1917. Then visit the Mellah (Jewish Quarter) and its historic synagogues. Spend the late afternoon at the Jardin Majorelle — a vivid cobalt-blue botanical garden once owned by Yves Saint Laurent, now a tranquil escape from the city bustle.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a traditional hammam experience at a mid-range local hammam (such as Hammam de la Rose or Les Bains de Marrakech) — a quintessential Moroccan cultural ritual involving steam, black soap scrub, and relaxation. End the evening with dinner in the Mellah area.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a local café near the Medina serving msemen (Moroccan flatbread), amlou (almond-argan dip), and coffee
meals.lunch: Nomad Restaurant near the Saadian Tombs — contemporary Moroccan cuisine with a rooftop terrace, great for a mid-day break (approx. 100–180 MAD)
meals.dinner: Riad Yima or a local riad restaurant in the Mellah — intimate setting, Moroccan home-style cooking, try the mrouzia (sweet lamb tagine) (approx. 150–220 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: Book the Jardin Majorelle tickets online in advance (approx. 150 MAD entry). Hammam sessions should also be booked ahead — budget around 200–400 MAD for a mid-range experience with a scrub and massage. March weather in Marrakech is pleasant (18–24°C), ideal for outdoor exploration.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early (around 7:00–8:00 AM) from Marrakech by private transfer or shared shuttle heading toward the Sahara Desert via the scenic Dades Valley route. Cross the dramatic High Atlas Mountains through the Tizi n'Tichka pass (2,260m elevation) — stop for photos at the summit. Visit the UNESCO-listed Aït Benhaddou ksar (fortified village), a stunning earthen citadel used as a filming location for Game of Thrones and Gladiator.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the journey through the Valley of Roses (Vallée des Roses) and the Draa Valley, passing palm groves and ancient kasbahs. Stop in Ouarzazate — the 'Hollywood of Africa' — for a brief visit to the Atlas Film Studios or the Taourirt Kasbah. Continue east toward Erfoud or Merzouga (gateway to the Erg Chebbi dunes).
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at your desert camp near Merzouga by late afternoon/early evening. Mount camels for a sunset camel trek into the Erg Chebbi dunes — one of Morocco's most iconic experiences. Watch the sun melt behind the golden dunes. Overnight in a comfortable mid-range desert camp with traditional Berber tent accommodation.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at hotel before departure — or packed breakfast from hotel
meals.lunch: Restaurant stop in Aït Benhaddou or Ouarzazate — try a Berber omelet, harira soup, or a simple tagine at a roadside restaurant (approx. 60–100 MAD)
meals.dinner: Traditional Berber dinner at the desert camp — included in most camp packages: harira, tagine, Moroccan salads, bread, and mint tea under the stars

day_by_day.notes: This is a long travel day (approximately 8–10 hours of driving with stops). Depart as early as possible. Book a reputable private driver or organized tour for this route — costs range from 800–1,500 MAD for a shared tour or 1,500–2,500 MAD for a private transfer. Bring layers — desert nights in March can drop to 5–10°C. Camel trek is typically 1–2 hours each way.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up before sunrise (around 6:00 AM) to climb the dunes on foot for a breathtaking Sahara sunrise — one of the most magical experiences in Morocco. Watch the light shift across the endless sea of sand. Return to camp for a traditional Berber breakfast. Explore the Merzouga village and the edge of the Erg Chebbi dunes on foot or by 4x4.
day_by_day.afternoon: Optional adventure activities: quad biking across the dunes, sandboarding on the slopes of Erg Chebbi, or a 4x4 off-road excursion to visit a nomadic Berber family encampment and learn about desert life. Visit the nearby fossil and mineral shops in Erfoud — the region is famous for Devonian-era marine fossils.
day_by_day.evening: Begin the return journey toward the Draa Valley or stay one more night at the desert camp (if itinerary allows). If returning, stop in Tinghir to visit the spectacular Todra Gorge — towering 300-meter limestone cliffs carved by the Todra River, perfect for a short hike or walk through the gorge. Overnight in Tinghir or a nearby guesthouse.

meals.breakfast: Berber breakfast at desert camp — khobz bread, olive oil, honey, argan oil, Moroccan tea, and eggs
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch in the dunes or a simple meal at a local café in Merzouga village (approx. 50–80 MAD)
meals.dinner: Local restaurant or guesthouse in Tinghir — try a slow-cooked lamb tagine with prunes or a vegetable couscous (approx. 80–130 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: Quad biking costs approximately 200–350 MAD per hour. Sandboards can be rented at the camp. Sunrise climb requires an early alarm — it's absolutely worth it. Sunscreen, sunglasses, and a headscarf or hat are essential in the desert. The Todra Gorge is accessible and beautiful in March.

day_by_day.morning: Depart from Tinghir and travel through the scenic Dades Gorge — a dramatic canyon with winding roads and rose-red rock formations. Stop at the 'Road of a Thousand Kasbahs' for photos and a short walk. Continue through the Skoura Oasis, a lush palm grove dotted with ancient kasbahs, including the well-preserved Kasbah Amridil.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return through Ouarzazate and begin the ascent back over the High Atlas Mountains. Stop at a Berber village along the route for tea and a glimpse into mountain life. If time allows, visit the Telouet Kasbah — a crumbling but atmospheric former palace of the powerful Glaoui clan, accessible via a scenic detour from the main pass.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back in Marrakech by early evening (approximately 6:00–7:00 PM). Check back into Aegean Bliss Resort. Freshen up and head out for a final relaxed evening in the Medina — browse the night souks for last-minute souvenirs or gifts. Enjoy a special farewell dinner at a quality Marrakech restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse breakfast in Tinghir — traditional Moroccan spread
meals.lunch: Roadside stop in the Dades Valley or Ouarzazate — simple Berber café with tagine and bread (approx. 60–100 MAD)
meals.dinner: Dar Moha or La Maison Arabe in Marrakech — upscale but accessible mid-range dining experience in a stunning riad setting, featuring refined Moroccan cuisine (approx. 200–350 MAD per person)

day_by_day.notes: The return drive from Tinghir to Marrakech takes approximately 5–6 hours with stops. An early morning departure (7:00 AM) is recommended. The Telouet Kasbah detour adds about 1.5 hours but is highly rewarding for history lovers. Book the farewell dinner in advance as popular riads fill up quickly.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a final leisurely breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort. Depending on your departure time, take a gentle morning walk through the Medina one last time — pick up any remaining souvenirs such as argan oil, Moroccan spices, leather slippers (babouches), or handwoven textiles. Visit a local patisserie for a final Moroccan pastry and coffee.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the hotel. Transfer to Marrakech Menara Airport for your departure flight. Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for check-in and security.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Marrakech — carry the memories of the Medina's labyrinthine souks, Saharan sunrises, and Berber hospitality with you.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort — savor it!
meals.lunch: Light lunch near the Medina or at a café such as Café de France on Djemaa el-Fna square — a classic people-watching spot for a final Moroccan coffee and pastry (approx. 40–80 MAD)
meals.dinner: Airport dining or in-flight meal

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your departure flight time and arrange airport transfer the night before. Moroccan customs allow you to take argan oil, spices, and crafts — but avoid purchasing items made from protected animal products. Currency exchange: convert remaining MAD back to your home currency at the airport or a city exchange bureau before departing. Tipping is customary — budget 10–15 MAD for porters and small service tips.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Morocco (Marrakech and Sahara) Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, Morocco (Marrakech and Sahara)

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled – flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled – in transit
day_by_day.evening: Private airport transfer arranged by Aegean Bliss Resort. Upon arrival at Marrakech Menara Airport, a dedicated concierge meets you with a welcome drink and assists with luggage. Settle into your Beachfront suite, enjoy a late-night welcome amenity prepared by the resort (Moroccan mint tea, dates, and pastries in-room).

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (in transit)
meals.lunch: Not applicable (in transit)
meals.dinner: Late-night in-room dining: traditional Moroccan mezze platter with harira soup, msemen flatbread, and seasonal sweets arranged by the resort kitchen upon request

day_by_day.notes: Arrival is late at night. Keep Day 1 light — focus on a smooth check-in and rest. Confirm all upcoming excursions with the resort concierge before sleeping. Unpack and prepare for an early start on Day 2.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely breakfast at the resort, then a private guided tour of the UNESCO-listed Medina of Marrakech. Explore the iconic Djemaa el-Fna square in its calm morning hours, visit the ornate Koutoubia Mosque gardens, and wander through the historic Mellah (Jewish Quarter). Your private guide provides deep cultural and historical context.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the stunning Bahia Palace — a 19th-century masterpiece of Moroccan-Andalusian architecture — followed by a curated tour of the Saadian Tombs, the royal necropolis dating to the 16th century. Enjoy a private transfer between sites in an air-conditioned luxury vehicle.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on a rooftop terrace overlooking the Medina skyline. Dinner at a top-tier Marrakech restaurant inside a restored riad, featuring a multi-course Moroccan tasting menu with sommelier-paired Moroccan wines.

meals.breakfast: Full à la carte breakfast at the resort — fresh-squeezed orange juice, Moroccan crepes (msemen), eggs, local cheeses, honey, argan oil, and premium coffee
meals.lunch: Private lunch at a heritage riad restaurant in the Medina — slow-cooked lamb tagine with preserved lemon and olives, Moroccan salad spread, and fresh bread
meals.dinner: Dinner at a premium riad restaurant (e.g., Le Foundouk or Dar Yacout style) — bastilla au pigeon, slow-braised lamb with ras el hanout, and orange-blossom crème brûlée for dessert

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes for Medina exploration. The souks can be overwhelming — your private guide will help navigate. Tipping guides is customary (approx. 100–200 MAD). Book dinner reservations in advance through the concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Private visit to the legendary Majorelle Garden — the cobalt-blue botanical paradise co-restored by Yves Saint Laurent — timed early to beat the crowds. Includes access to the Berber Museum within the estate. Stroll through the lush gardens with a personal guide explaining the rare plant species and artistic history.
day_by_day.afternoon: Guided luxury souk experience: explore the labyrinthine markets with a personal shopper/guide. Visit specialist artisan workshops for hand-woven carpets, hand-tooled leather goods, silver jewelry, and spice bazaars. Enjoy a private demonstration by master craftsmen. Opportunity for curated, high-quality souvenir purchases.
day_by_day.evening: Indulge in a 2-hour premium traditional hammam and spa ritual at one of Marrakech's finest hammams (e.g., a private hammam session at La Mamounia Spa or Royal Mansour Spa). Black soap scrub, ghassoul clay mask, and argan oil massage included. Return to the resort for a relaxed evening.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — Moroccan-style spread with amlou (almond-argan dip), fresh fruit, yogurt, and pastries
meals.lunch: Lunch at a chic café near Majorelle Garden — avocado toast with local herbs, grilled vegetable couscous, and fresh juices
meals.dinner: Intimate dinner at the resort's signature restaurant or a nearby fine-dining establishment — seafood pastilla, Moroccan-spiced sea bass, and honey-pistachio dessert

day_by_day.notes: Book the hammam session in advance through the concierge. Bring a small bag for souk purchases. The Majorelle Garden has an entrance fee (~70 MAD); private access arrangements can be made through the resort for quieter visits.

day_by_day.morning: Early departure by private luxury 4x4 vehicle to the High Atlas Mountains (approx. 1 hour from Marrakech). Visit the Ourika Valley — dramatic mountain scenery, Berber villages, and terraced farmland. Guided trek to a local waterfall with a knowledgeable mountain guide. Experience authentic Berber village life and traditional architecture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Lunch hosted by a Berber family in their mountain home — a rare, immersive cultural experience. Afterwards, visit the Kasbah du Toubkal area or the village of Asni for panoramic Atlas views. Optional mule ride through mountain trails for the adventurous. Return to Marrakech by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner drinks at the resort or a nearby rooftop bar. Relaxed evening with a private in-room dinner option or a quiet dinner at a local neighborhood restaurant favored by Marrakchi locals rather than tourists.

meals.breakfast: Early packed gourmet breakfast prepared by the resort for the road — pastries, fruit, coffee thermos, and Moroccan flatbread with cheese
meals.lunch: Authentic Berber home-cooked lunch — freshly baked bread, multiple tagines, couscous with seven vegetables, mint tea, and seasonal fruit
meals.dinner: Dinner at a local Marrakchi neighborhood restaurant — mechoui (whole slow-roasted lamb), Moroccan salads, and chebakia (honey-sesame cookies) with mint tea

day_by_day.notes: Wear layered clothing as Atlas Mountain temperatures can be cooler than Marrakech, especially in March. Comfortable hiking shoes are essential. The Berber family lunch is a private arrangement — confirm with the concierge. Altitude at some stops can reach 1,500–2,000m.

day_by_day.date: Day 5 – March 19, 2027 (Journey to the Sahara – Draa Valley)
day_by_day.morning: Early luxury vehicle departure toward the Sahara Desert (approx. 8–9 hours with stops, or 45-minute private charter flight option). En route, stop at the dramatic Tizi n'Tichka mountain pass (2,260m elevation) — stunning panoramic photo opportunity. Continue through the Draa Valley, lined with ancient kasbahs and palm oases.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the fortified UNESCO-listed Ksar of Aït Benhaddou — one of Morocco's most spectacular earthen architecture sites, used as a backdrop for films like Gladiator and Game of Thrones. Private guided tour with a historian. Continue to the Draa Valley oases and arrive at the desert camp vicinity by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at a premium luxury desert camp near Merzouga or Zagora. Check into a lavish Berber-style tent with en-suite facilities, private terrace, and desert views. Camel trek into the Erg Chebbi dunes at sunset — a golden-hour experience. Stargazing session with a professional astronomer guide around the camp bonfire.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast before departure — energizing spread to fuel the journey
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic lunch at Aït Benhaddou — prepared by the resort: artisan sandwiches, salads, fruit, and sparkling water served with a view of the kasbah
meals.dinner: Traditional Saharan dinner under the stars at the luxury camp — Berber music performance, lamb mechoui cooked in earthen pit, couscous, roasted vegetables, and Moroccan pastries; premium Moroccan wine available

day_by_day.notes: The road journey is long but scenic — consider the private charter flight option for comfort (arrange through concierge). Pack a light jacket for desert nights, which can be cold in March (temperatures can drop to 5–10°C). Confirm the luxury camp booking includes private en-suite tents with heating.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn wake-up for a private sunrise camel or horseback ride to the peak of the highest dune. Watch the sun rise over the Erg Chebbi sand sea — one of Morocco's most breathtaking natural spectacles. Return to camp for a leisurely breakfast. Optional sandboarding on the dunes with equipment provided by the camp.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the nearby oasis village of Merzouga with a private guide — visit a local nomadic family, learn about traditional desert survival techniques, and experience a private Gnawa music session (a trance-based musical tradition). Visit a fossil and mineral artisan workshop unique to the desert region. Rest and relax at the camp during the hottest part of the afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Private sundowner cocktail setup atop a dune — champagne and Moroccan appetizers served by camp staff as the desert turns amber and crimson. Return to camp for a final Saharan dinner with a private Berber storytelling session around the fire. Sleep under the stars in your luxury tent.

meals.breakfast: Lavish camp breakfast — fresh-baked msemen, local honey, argan oil, eggs, fruit, Moroccan coffee, and fresh-squeezed juice served on your private tent terrace
meals.lunch: Light desert lunch at the camp — chilled gazpacho, Moroccan mezze, grilled chicken skewers, and fresh lemonade with rose water
meals.dinner: Gourmet Saharan feast — slow-cooked kefta tagine, vegetable couscous, pastilla au poulet, and a dessert of dates stuffed with almond paste, accompanied by premium Moroccan rosé wine

day_by_day.notes: Apply high-SPF sunscreen during daytime dune activities. Sandboarding equipment is typically provided by luxury camps. The Gnawa music session is a culturally significant experience — tip the musicians generously (200–300 MAD). Stay hydrated throughout the day — the camp should provide unlimited water.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise moment at the desert camp. Leisurely farewell breakfast. Private luxury vehicle or charter flight departure back toward Marrakech. En route, stop at the ancient city of Ouarzazate — the 'Hollywood of Africa' — and visit the Atlas Corporation Studios or the 17th-century Taourirt Kasbah for a final dose of Moroccan history.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Marrakech. Freshen up at the resort. Last-minute luxury shopping in the Gueliz neighborhood (Marrakech's modern district) — visit high-end Moroccan design boutiques for premium argan products, designer caftans, and artisan crafts. Alternatively, enjoy a final spa treatment at the resort.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at Marrakech's most celebrated fine-dining restaurant — a lavish multi-course experience celebrating Moroccan gastronomy at its finest. Toast to an unforgettable journey. Private transfer to Marrakech Menara Airport if departing, or a final night of rest at the resort.

meals.breakfast: Final desert camp breakfast — a celebratory spread with Moroccan pancakes, fresh fruit platter, artisan cheeses, and premium coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch in Ouarzazate — grilled merguez sausages, Moroccan salads, and fresh bread at a charming local restaurant with kasbah views
meals.dinner: Grand farewell dinner at a top Marrakech restaurant (e.g., La Grande Table Marocaine at Royal Mansour or equivalent) — seven-course Moroccan tasting menu with wine pairing, ending with traditional mint tea ceremony

day_by_day.notes: Confirm return flight details and airport transfer timing with the resort concierge. Allow at least 3 hours before any international departure for Marrakech airport check-in. The Gueliz boutiques are a great alternative to Medina souks for fixed-price, high-quality Moroccan goods. Settle all tips and gratuities before departure — budget approximately 500–1,000 MAD total for guides, drivers, and camp staff across the trip.
